name: Lost Kingdoms Beyond the Mediterranean
description: Gold empires of the Sahel, stone cities of Zimbabwe, temples of Angkor and the Andes: kingdoms outside Europe that history books often skip.

checkpoints.name: Early kingdoms
checkpoints.note: Elam and Urartu rise in the highlands of Asia, Kush rules on the Nile, and Aksum trades across the Red Sea. In Mexico and Guatemala the Maya begin building their cities.

checkpoints.name: Golden roads and temples
checkpoints.note: Ghana grows rich on gold and salt, Srivijaya controls the sea lanes of Southeast Asia, and Angkor raises its temples. Korea has its own kingdom of Goryeo while Benin and Ife make bronze art.

checkpoints.name: Courts of gold and sun
checkpoints.note: Mali and Songhai make Timbuktu famous, Great Zimbabwe builds in stone, and Majapahit and Ayutthaya rule much of Southeast Asia. The Aztecs and the Incas build great empires before Spanish ships arrive.

checkpoints.name: The last kingdoms
checkpoints.note: Dahomey, Ashanti, Oyo and the Zulu hold off outsiders for a time, and Ethiopia wins at Adwa. Colonial wars and conquest end one kingdom after another, from Benin to Hawaii.
